nextStoryContext: US-R6-002 fixed the fd leak the reviewer found in makeSpawnSidecarFn (src/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.ts): the closure returned by makeSpawnSidecarFn openSync'd a fresh log fd on EVERY invocation (every respawn attempt) but never closed it, and because handleOneTick resets state.attempts to 0 whenever the sidecar is observed alive again, a flapping sidecar could accumulate descriptors without bound over a long-lived watcher session. Mechanical 1-file fix per the story's own notes: added `closeSync(logFd)` immediately after the `Bun.spawn(...)` call inside the closure, so the parent's copy is released as soon as the child has its own duplicated descriptor. Verified empirically (not just by reading Bun's docs) with a standalone bun -e script: 5x openSync+Bun.spawn+closeSync cycles reused the SAME fd number each time (proof the close actually took effect), vs the reviewer's prior probe showing 5 distinct fds all still open without the fix. Step 5.5: fetched bun.sh/docs/api/spawn -- confirms passing a `number` for stdout/stderr just means 'write to the file with the given file descriptor', with no mention of the parent's copy being closed automatically, consistent with posix_spawn dup semantics and the empirical probe. Deliberately did NOT touch spawnSidecarDefault (src/commands/run.ts): it runs once per `cam run` invocation (not from inside a long-lived poll loop), so its single fd is bounded by the process lifetime and is out of this story's scope (the story's notes explicitly contrast it with the liveness-watch closure as the one that's fine). Deliberately did NOT add a new regression test for the production makeSpawnSidecarFn closure itself: the existing test/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.test.ts always injects a fake spawnSidecarFn (never constructs the real production default), and per prd.json there is a SEPARATE story, US-R6-003, whose whole scope is exactly this gap ("the US-R4-001 regression test doesn't call the actual production makeSpawnSidecarFn closure") -- adding that coverage here would step on US-R6-003's scope. Full quality spine green: typecheck 0 errors, bun test 5935 pass/0 fail (unchanged count -- no tests needed updating since no test constructs the real closure), bun run check:all all-green (lint/file-size/debt-markers/version-skips/coverage/dead-code/dup/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/skip-ratchet), no file-size budget edit needed. Appended one patterns.md bullet under the sidecar/CAM-482 thread capturing the durable lesson: Bun.spawn's number-fd stdio option never closes/owns the caller's descriptor, so any future per-invocation openSync inside a long-lived loop needs the same closeSync-right-after-spawn treatment. Remaining CAM-482 finding not yet addressed: US-R6-003 (missing regression coverage for the real makeSpawnSidecarFn closure) -- still passes:false, next in line for whichever story the supervisor dispatches.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed passing a number for stdout/stderr writes to that fd without closing/duplicating away the caller's copy; matches the empirical fd-reuse probe and justifies the closeSync fix.
